title: Jenny Lind soup
html_source: One of the most celebrated opera performers of the nineteenth century, Swedish-born Jenny Lind (1820–1887) dazzled European and American audiences with her radiant soprano voice and with an image that emphasized wholesomeness and purity. A soup was invented and often partaken of by the celebrated cantatrice. The dish is made from mashed rutabaga or sago, chicken stock thickened with a roux, Gruyère cheese, sage, egg yolks, heavy cream, and topped with beaten egg whites.
